how much they wanted. And they said:
"Twenty zūzē."
And when he was afraid,
he brought them what they had demanded,
and said
that they should take the coins through the crack of the door.
And they said:
"No,
but open the door to us."
And while they were persisting in this dispute for about an hour,
their companions climbed up from the walls to the roof,
and went down into the house and opened the door,
and those others also entered.
And they tortured the Jew,
until he showed them all the property that he possessed.
And when they stretched out a hand against him to kill him,
his wife threw herself upon him and began to persuade those bandits, saying:
"Spare this man's youth,
and kill me instead of him."
Those accursed ones, however, in the hardness of their hearts, answered her:
"We will kill both him and you!"
And when they had slaughtered her husband,
they also inflicted blows with dagger strokes upon her,
and left her half dead,
and took much property and went away.
And when morning dawned,
and people came,
they found the Jew slaughtered,
and his wife at her last gasp.
And when she had recounted what had happened,
she died at about nine o'clock.
At this time, some men from among the Arab poor (faqirs), about thirty persons, entered the country of Cilicia from the region of Syria,
as if to receive a blessing from the grave of Caliph al-Ma'mūn,
who was buried in Tarsus.
And the suspicion arose
that Bunduqdār, the lord of Egypt, was among them,
having disguised himself and gone about to spy out the rest of the kingdoms.
And the ruler of Cilicia laid a hand upon them,
and seized them and imprisoned them in the Great Fortress.
And when the news flew to Egypt,
envoys began to arrive continuously with requests for those who had been imprisoned.
And thus that suspicion came close to being confirmed,
and King Leon did not wish to release them.
And an army of the Egyptians gathered and entered Cilicia during the days of the Great Fast,
in the year 1586 [of the Greeks = 1275 AD].
And there were {OCR?}
about five hundred horsemen.
And an army of the Armenians encountered them,
and put them to flight.
And again a mighty army of about eight thousand gathered,
and burst upon that miserable country.
And they reached Ayas in the deep twilight of Monday in the Week of Miracles, on the 25th
of Adar.
